verdict.rationale: Pipecat's own interruptions docs say that on barge-in the bot stops immediately, in-flight work is cancelled, and the pipeline is ready for the new user input. That covers stopping speech and recovering the turn, and Pipecat Cloud adds Krisp filtering against false interruptions. The evidence never shows how conversation context is updated after an interruption, such as truncating the assistant message to what was actually spoken. Missing for 10: documented context updating on interruption, independent or hands-on corroboration of barge-in behavior.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the agent to handle interruptions (barge-in) gracefully — stopping speech, updating context, and recovering the turn

citations.quote: Interruptions (also called barge-in) let the user talk over the bot. When the user starts speaking while the bot is talking, the bot stops immediately, in-flight work is cancelled
the pipeline is ready for the new user input
Eliminates background noise and voices that cause false interruptions, powered by Krisp.
